SCRAP_WEIGHT_FACTOR: ---------------------------------------------------------------- SCRAPS (a modifier)
Scraps are a MODIFIER on a food, not one shared pile: eating a unit of a food with
`leaves_scraps` leaves that fraction behind as "<food>_scraps" (pork -> pork_scraps). Each scrap
item derives its values from its source -- lighter, cheaper, and quicker to spoil -- and is still
food, so it can be fed to animals that eat scraps (pigs, dogs) or eaten by people who cannot
afford better. Generic "scraps" (kitchen leavings) remains animal feed only.
scraps are bone, rind, skin: half the weight per unit of the cut

SCRAP_SCARCITY_FACTOR: and worth a small fraction of it

SCRAP_DECAY: scraps spoil faster than any whole food (perishable class is 0.25)

NITROGEN: ---------------------------------------------------------------- THE NITROGEN CYCLE
Each land parcel holds soil nitrogen (`nitrogen` on the Land node), in units per unit of area:
  in:   SOILS[...]["nitrogen"] at the start; `mineralisation` each period (organic matter slowly
        releasing N, plus rain); legume `fixes`; and fertiliser a farmer spreads (any item with a
        `nitrogen` tag -- manure, compost, dung -- via the `fertilise` action).
  out:  each growing bed's `nitrogen` demand (carried off in the harvest), and `leaching` -- a
        fraction of the parcel's N lost each period, scaled by the soil's drainage.
  loop: people eat the harvest -> night soil at the latrine -> composted (make_compost) -> spread;
        livestock eat pasture -> manure -> spread; burnt fuel -> ash -> compost.
A bed whose demand was fully met yields its full `yield`; one that got none yields `yield_floor`
of it. Beds not on a land parcel (small test fixtures) are unaffected.
the INPUT_TYPES slot the fertilise action draws on
nitrogen spread per fertilise action
farmers offer to fertilise a plot below this fraction of capacity
...and sow a restorative legume below this fraction

LABOUR_RATE: reference value per MINUTE of labour (an hour of work ~ 1.2 in coin units)

TRAIN_HEADROOM: the trained part of strength or stamina builds up to 0.4 x base, so effective strength and stamina top out at base x 1.4 (ceiling = base x TRAIN_HEADROOM). Source: the 0.4 literal in seeds/bigville_body.json, rules bd_train_strength and bd_train_stamina (the seed's own design figure; no real-world source consulted).

TRAIN_RATE: fraction of the remaining gap one effort closes at intensity 1 (an effort of intensity x closes x * TRAIN_RATE of it). Source: the 0.12 literal in seeds/bigville_body.json, rules bd_train_strength and bd_train_stamina (seed design figure; no real-world source consulted, so APPROX as to real training rates).

HUNGER_PER_STAMINA: Exertion also makes you HUNGRIER: the hunger gained per unit of stamina spent, in loaf units (hunger is counted in meals of one loaf, see ITEMS feeds). Modest: a heavy recipe (stamina_cost ~0.4) adds ~0.08 of a loaf-meal, so hard work needs more food over a day, not instantly. 0.2 is the Phase 022 value of 1.0 on the old scale, where a meal relieved about 5 hunger (1.0 / 5). Phase 027 later made a meal one loaf and left this constant at 1.0, which made exertion five times too hungry (fix024). APPROX: derived from the old design's figures, no real-world source. Raises the SAME hunger_level the sustenance drive reads; EATING (not buying) relieves it.
